study.title: Geomorphological evidence of near-surface ice at candidate landing sites in northern Amazonis Planitia, Mars
study.authors: Luzzi, E., Heldmann, J.L., Williams, K.E., Nodjoumi, G., Deutsch, A., Sehlke, A.
study.journal: Journal of Geophysical Research: Planets, 130(5), e2024JE008724 (2025)

AP-1.summary: Knobby polygonal terrain covers most of the area, with smooth polygonal terrain, expanded and inverted expanded craters, pingo-like features and arcuate ridges. Brain coral terrain lies about 8 km southeast, outside the mapped area.

AP-8.summary: Smooth polygonal terrain dominates, with knobby polygonal terrain in the west. Features include dense clusters of expanded craters, inverted expanded craters, arcuate ridges and a terraced crater with brain coral terrain about 1.4 km from the site. No pingo-like features.

AP-9.summary: Entirely knobby polygonal terrain, with expanded craters, inverted expanded craters and pingo-like features. No brain coral terrain or arcuate ridges.

feature_classes.name: Expanded secondary crater
feature_classes.description: Secondary impact craters that have been enlarged and degraded. They are elongated, with expanded rims and a sharp, preserved scarp facing northeast; floors are covered by polygons and no ejecta is visible. Inner morphology varies: a bowl-shaped central pit ("bullseye"), a central bulge, or a flat floor. Major axes range from about 20 to 503 m and floor depths from about 1 to 18 m.
feature_classes.ice_significance: Expansion happens when sublimation removes buried excess ice after an impact, so these craters indicate that significant excess ice is present, or was present, in the ground.

feature_classes.name: Mound
feature_classes.description: Small positive-relief mound mapped as its own class, separate from pingo-like features.
feature_classes.ice_significance: No specific ice interpretation is given for this class.

feature_classes.name: Pingo-like feature
feature_classes.description: Prominent subcircular-to-elongated rounded mounds that rise above the flat surrounding terrain and carry the same polygonal surface. Elongated examples are 196-442 m long and 4-10 m high; subcircular ones are 117-440 m across and 4-8 m high. Some have a shallow summit depression. They appear randomly distributed with no preferred alignment.
feature_classes.ice_significance: Their size and shape resemble terrestrial pingos (ice-cored mounds), but this cannot be confirmed from morphology alone; they could also be heavily degraded inverted expanded craters.

feature_classes.name: Polygonized terrain B (smooth polygonal terrain)
feature_classes.description: Low-albedo terrain of smooth high-centered polygons where knobs are rare. It is affected by a dense population of arcuate ridges that trend northwest-southeast.
feature_classes.ice_significance: Thermal contraction polygons, indicating shallow ground ice (tens of cm below the surface).

feature_classes.name: Hummocky unit
feature_classes.ice_significance: No specific ice interpretation is given for this class.

feature_classes.name: Polygonized terrain A (knobby polygonal terrain)
feature_classes.description: Low-albedo terrain of high-centered polygons (raised centers, depressed margins), with knobs at the center of some polygons that give a domical look. Knobby polygons are typically 0.5-1.6 m high. At AP-1 it covers most of the area and lies topographically higher than the smooth polygonal terrain.
feature_classes.ice_significance: Thermal contraction polygons; the ice beneath them is estimated to lie on the order of tens of cm below the surface, shallow enough to be reachable for resource use.

feature_classes.name: Brain coral terrain
feature_classes.description: Anastomosing sets of ridges and troughs with high albedo, in contact with smooth polygonal terrain and topographically lower than it. Here it is open-cell: narrow sinuous ridges (6-14 m wide) enclosing depressed flat-floored cells (3-14.5 m wide), with about 1 m of relief.
feature_classes.ice_significance: Widespread at Mars' mid-latitudes; its origin is debated, with leading explanations involving sublimation of ground ice.

feature_classes.name: Crater floor
feature_classes.description: Floor of the impact crater mapped at AP-8.

feature_classes.name: Crater wall
feature_classes.description: Wall of the terraced impact crater near AP-8. Its polygonal patterned ground matches the polygons on the surrounding plain.
feature_classes.ice_significance: Polygons continuing across the crater walls indicate the ice-related patterned ground is widespread.

feature_classes.name: Domical polygonized terrain (knobby polygonal terrain)
feature_classes.description: Low-albedo, knobby high-centered polygonal terrain. At AP-9 it covers the entire mapped region; no smooth polygonal terrain was identified there.
feature_classes.ice_significance: Thermal contraction polygons, indicating shallow ground ice (tens of cm below the surface).

feature_classes.name: Inverted expanded secondary crater
feature_classes.description: Expanded craters whose relief has flipped to positive. Advanced examples are flat-topped mounds 3-6 m high with steep flanks; early-stage examples are flat and ringed by a ridge. All show radial, concentric and orthogonal fractures, and some have a central bulge.
feature_classes.ice_significance: Evidence of ongoing sublimation-driven change of ice-rich ground, since they are expanded craters that have undergone topographic inversion.

feature_classes.name: Knobby polygonal terrain
feature_classes.description: Knobby high-centered polygonal terrain, present only in the western part of the AP-8 area.
feature_classes.ice_significance: Thermal contraction polygons, indicating shallow ground ice.

feature_classes.name: Smooth polygonal terrain
feature_classes.description: Smooth high-centered polygonal terrain that dominates the AP-8 area. Arcuate ridges occur mainly within it.
feature_classes.ice_significance: Thermal contraction polygons, indicating shallow ground ice.

feature_classes.name: Terrace
feature_classes.description: Terrace of the ~650 m terraced impact crater near AP-8, about 10-20 m below the surrounding plain. Most of it is covered by open-cell brain coral terrain.
feature_classes.ice_significance: Hosts the brain coral terrain at AP-8.

contact_classes.name: Certain contact
contact_classes.description: Boundary between units that can be traced confidently.

contact_classes.name: Inferred contact
contact_classes.description: Boundary between units placed by interpretation where the contact is gradational or not clearly visible.
